content: Plasma volume is notably reduced in women diagnosed with pre-eclampsia. This observation has led to the hypothesis that increasing plasma volume might enhance maternal and uteroplacental blood flow, potentially improving outcomes for both the mother and her baby. The objective of this review was to evaluate the effects of plasma volume expansion as a treatment for women with pre-eclampsia. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted in the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register and the Cochrane Controlled Trials Register (Issue 4, 2000). The search was later updated on October 1, 2009, and the results were added to the awaiting classification section for further assessment. The review included only randomized trials, excluding quasi-randomized designs. Participants were pregnant women with hypertension, with or without proteinuria. Women who were already postpartum at the time of trial entry were excluded. The interventions assessed involved comparisons between plasma volume expansion and no expansion, or comparisons between different types of plasma volume expanders. Data extraction was performed independently by two reviewers, and any discrepancies were resolved through discussion. There was no blinding of the authorship or the results during the review process. The review included three trials involving a total of 61 women. All of these trials compared the use of a colloid solution for plasma volume expansion with no plasma volume expansion. For every outcome reported, the confidence intervals were extremely wide and crossed the line of no effect, indicating a lack of statistical significance. The authors concluded that there is insufficient evidence to provide reliable estimates of the effects of plasma volume expansion for women with pre-eclampsia. It is important to note that the 14 citations in the awaiting classification section of the review may influence the conclusions once they are fully assessed.
